label: rem:hausdorff-dimension-classical-comparison
title: Classical Hausdorff dimension $d_H$ of the Julia set vs. the $q$-deformed $d_{H,q}$
html:
Remark. Classical Hausdorff dimension d_H of the Julia set vs. the q-deformed d_{H,q}

The q-deformed Hausdorff dimension d_{H,q} = (2q-1)^2/q^3 (discrete recurrence) differs from the classical Hausdorff dimension d_H of the Julia set J(f_q) over \mathbb{C}.

d_{H,q} vs. d_H: comparison with classical Hausdorff dimension. For parameters c(\varTheta) on the main cardioid of the Mandelbrot set, the Julia set is a quasicircle. The classical Hausdorff dimension d_H satisfies:

  1. Ruelle perturbative (valid for |c| \ll 1): d_H = 1 + \frac{|c(\varTheta)|^2}{4 \ln 2} + O(|c|^4). At \varTheta = 0.1097: |c| = 0.346, yielding d_H \approx 1.043.
  2. Transfer operator (numerical, Bowen--Ruelle): d_H \approx 1.047 at N = 800 grid points.
  3. QOU q-deformed: d_{H,q} = 1.088.

The gap d_{H,q} - d_H \approx 0.041 arises from differing Manning--McCluskey inputs. See Table 2.

The classical d_H arises from conformal dynamics over \mathbb{C}. The q-deformed d_{H,q} replaces the transcendental \ln 2 with the rational \eta_q, and the numerical \chi(c) with the algebraic \chi_q. We propose that d_{H,q} governs the physical regime.

No closed form exists for the classical d_H(J_c) over the main cardioid parameter c. It appears implicitly as the unique zero of the Bowen--Ruelle pressure function P(-t\log|f_c'|) = 0.
